title: Question: Is it able to use lightningcss as a parser from node?
fixedBy: bda77f3 'Add support for StyleSheet visitor function' (v1.23.0, 2024-01-14)
impact: 3 reactions; use cases in comments: an ESLint CSS parser and a Stylelint-style typed-value linter (jacobrask's fork). Maintainer answered in 2023 that a full parse() wasn't offered for performance reasons.
code: node/ast.d.ts: StyleSheet, Location2 (rules have loc; declarations do not)
summary: There is still no `parse()` export, but since 1.23.0 a `StyleSheet` visitor receives the whole typed AST, so `transform({code, visitor: {StyleSheet(s) { ast = s }}})` works as a parser. Parse errors on known syntax throw (strict) or become warnings with errorRecovery. Caveats for linters: transform still prints output, the whole AST crosses to JS (the cost the maintainer warned about), and declarations carry no source location (rules do, as `loc`).
repro: 440-repro.mjs: parse via StyleSheet visitor returns 2 rules (style, media), color parsed to {type:'rgb', r:255,...}, rule loc {line:0,column:1}; invalid media query throws. Correct on local, 1.33.0, 1.32.0, 1.31.1.
evidence: repro.mjs on local + 3 releases; 556-repro --range 1.18.0..1.33.0 shows the StyleSheet visitor first works in 1.23.0 (1.22.1 ignores it). StyleSheet visitor is not documented in website/pages/transforms.md (docs gap).

fix.approach: Optional: document the StyleSheet/StyleSheetExit visitors in website/pages/transforms.md with a parse example. Per-declaration locations would be a separate feature request (AST shape addition).

notVerified: Performance of whole-AST export vs PostCSS not measured.
